The AI selloff is not about demand evaporating. It is about cash flow, financing cost and how long the market is willing to wait for the returns.

Demand signals remain extremely strong.

SK hynix just reported Q3 revenue of 104.6 trillion won (+328% YoY) and operating profit of 83.3 trillion won with an ~80% margin. Management said DRAM and HBM volumes are effectively sold out through 2029, customer HBM requests are roughly double what they can supply, and they expect the supply shortage to persist through 2030. Long-term agreements already cover more than half of 2027–2028 capacity with 14 major customers. That is not a demand problem.⁠

Anthropic’s S-1 shows the unit economics at the model layer improving sharply. Revenue per dollar of compute and infrastructure expense rose from $0.40 in Q1 2025 to $2.08 in Q2 2026 - a 5.2× improvement in five quarters. Compute costs fell from 251% of revenue to 48%. The company generated its first quarterly operating profit. Revenue grew 1,368% YoY while compute expense rose only ~300%. Efficiency is rising, not collapsing.⁠

GPU rental prices have turned higher again. B200 on-demand rates rose more than 20% in a month in some indices; H100 and H200 also firmed. Tightness in the spot and short-term rental market is consistent with the hyperscalers’ own comments that they still cannot meet all the demand they see.⁠

On the supply side the hyperscalers themselves are not signalling a slowdown. Amazon maintained ~$220 billion 2026 cash cape

At the same time, $1.6 trillion of investment-grade corporate debt is coming due by 2031.

The corporate refinancing burden is becoming a major issue.

text:
Oct. 28: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh on AI sector financial conditions tightening. Iran War -> Energy prices -> inflation -> the discounting of forward rate policy matters.

"CHAIRMAN WARSH: Thank you, Claire. So, there was a narrative for quite a while, maybe even in this room over the course of the last several press conferences, well, they're going to raise rates, they're talking about raising rates, but it's not going to have any effect on AI, because the returns that investors are expecting are so different. I was skeptical of that view.

Interest rates get in the cracks, interest rates affect directly or indirectly, almost everything. And what have we seen? Since early September what we've seen inside of the technology complex, outside of the technology complex, whether you pronounce it AI or SI, Claire, is up to you, what have you seen?

Interest rates have had an effect. You've seen market participants that are discriminating between the kinds of investments they want to make. You've seen credit spreads for certain assets widen out, gap out. For others you've seen some tightening in financial conditions, but not significantly.

So on the thrust of your question of -- with respect to the new technology and this investment surge, do interest rates matter? I believe they do. And I don't believe that they're somehow divorced from the rest of the economy."

text:
Brent just printed $118 and the 10-year Treasury yield is at 4.94%. That relationship used to run the other way .

@robin_j_brooks is correct in this analysis. This is a regime shift, not a blip.

For most of 2026, oil up meant yields up. Inflation expectations fed straight into the long end. That link is now broken. The 20-day correlation between Brent and the 10Y has collapsed to its lowest since late 2024.

The reason is Europe. The French 10-year is at 4.96%, the highest since 2002. The spread over German Bunds has widened to 159bp, the widest since 2011. French debt-to-GDP is 117%, versus 90% at the last crisis peak.

Bessent confirmed this week that capital is leaving "concerning" jurisdictions and flowing into Treasuries as a safe haven. The US is catching a bid because the alternative is worse.

This is not a resolution of the fiscal problem. Net interest is still above $1 trillion. The term premium is being temporarily suppressed by a flight to quality, not by better US math.

If Europe stabilizes, the bid fades. If Europe cracks, the bid deepens.

text:
Binance lost about $6.3 billion in Thursday's hack. It is the largest crypto theft on record in dollar terms, roughly four times the $1.5 billion taken from Bybit in February 2025.

The drain started at 4:05 PM ET on Oct 29. TRM Labs says most of it left Binance wallets in about 20 minutes, across 10 blockchains.

Binance has set aside $6.34 billion to cover users. $5 billion of that is already held in the exact tokens that were stolen, about 80% of the loss. It is buying the rest through the market and OTC desks.

About $3 billion has been frozen on-chain, almost all of it $USDT and $USDC. The attacker still holds 18,270 $BTC split across 19 wallets. Elliptic says none of it has reached an exchange or service yet.

TRM and Chainalysis attribute the theft with high confidence to TraderTraitor, a North Korean state hacking unit. No government has confirmed it. Trump on Friday: "We don't know. We're looking at that." The FBI and Secret Service are both involved.

TRM counts $12.8 billion stolen by North Korea since 2017. $7.4 billion of it came this year.

Binance is targeting a phased restart of withdrawals early Sunday. Proof of reserves results are due Monday.

"So basically, you want to protect yourself against multiple scenarios."
